analysis.subject: biology
analysis.pageCoverage: Page introduces population genetics and the four evolutionary forces, defines population in biological and geographic terms, describes descriptive statistics for population data, and discusses why race and ethnicity are limited descriptors of human genetic variation.

overview.headline: How allele frequencies change and how human populations are described

keyPoints.point: Population genetics studies the distribution and change in allele frequencies under the influence of evolutionary forces.
keyPoints.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies under the influence of the four evolutionary forces

keyPoints.point: Descriptive statistics summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner.
keyPoints.quote: Descriptive statistics are used to summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner

keyPoints.point: In biology a population denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves.
keyPoints.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves

keyPoints.point: Research shows racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of genetic variation in the human species.
keyPoints.quote: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation in the human species

keyTerms.gloss: study of distribution and change in allele frequencies influenced by evolutionary forces
keyTerms.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies under the influence of the four evolutionary forces

keyTerms.gloss: distribution of gene variants and how their frequencies change within a population
keyTerms.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies under the influence of the four evolutionary forces

keyTerms.gloss: evolutionary force that changes allele frequencies through differential survival and reproduction
keyTerms.quote: four evolutionary forces: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration

keyTerms.gloss: methods to summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner
keyTerms.quote: Descriptive statistics are used to summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner

keyTerms.gloss: alternative grouping for classifying human populations when race categories are inadequate
keyTerms.quote: An alternative to classifying the human species by race is to divide them by ethnicity

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Compares definitions of population and grouping concepts so students distinguish biological, geographic, race and ethnicity uses.
componentPlan.focusQuote: The term "population" can be defined in many ways, but in the most common sense of the word, it is a collection of people or organisms

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Groups four evolutionary forces so students can sort examples by mechanism of allele frequency change.
componentPlan.focusQuote: four evolutionary forces: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks understanding of population definitions and misconceptions about race and genetic variation.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation in the human species
